newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco considers licensing group sex clubs.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco considers licensing group sex clubs.

text.p: San Francisco could become the first U.S. city to license group sex clubs, if proposed legislation is passed, a city newspaper reported on Friday.

Tom Ammiano, a member of the city's governing Board of Supervisors, is working on legislation that would have the city grant permits to businesses "that encourage patrons to engage in, or to watch other patrons engaging in, sexual activities," the San Francisco Chronicle said.
The proposal, still in draft form, must be passed by the Board of Supervisors before it becomes law.
One aim of the proposed legislation is to stop the spread of AIDS and other sexually transmitted diseases by regulating the sex clubs.
Sex clubs are large, open rooms where patrons pay between $5 and $20 to congregate for sex, masturbation and voyeurism, the Chronicle said.

It said that currently, there are six to eight mostly gay commercial sex clubs open daily to the public in San Francisco and a dozen or more private clubs that meet occasionally. The clubs are largely underground and unregulated, it said.
Under the proposed law, sex clubs would be required to provide condoms, lubricants, proper lighting and AIDS-prevention literature. The clubs would be subject to regular inspections.
Ammiano could not be reached for comment on Friday.
The proposal legislation is expected to be introduced in the San Francisco Board of Supervisors late this year or early 1997.
